case_name: Estate of Andrews, C. Appeal of:Winsor, J.

issues.label: Orphans' Court jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has subject-matter jurisdiction over the estate account, objections, and fee/commission approvals.

issues.label: Finality and appealability
issues.why: The court must determine which orders/decrees are final and thus appealable and whether the appeal was timely from the final decree.

issues.label: Scope of review on appeal
issues.why: The court must identify whether review is for abuse of discretion, error of law, or lack of evidentiary support in confirming an account and approving fees.

issues.label: Preservation/waiver of issues
issues.why: The court must decide whether objections and appellate issues were properly raised below and included in the Pa.R.A.P. 1925(b) statement.

issues.label: Standard for attorney fee reasonableness
issues.why: The court must apply Pennsylvania’s governing reasonableness test for estate legal fees (including LaRocca factors) rather than a purely customary percentage if required.

issues.label: Role of local fee guidelines
issues.why: The court must decide the legal effect of Donofrio/Washington County “guidelines” (prima facie benchmark vs controlling rule) and how they interact with statewide reasonableness law.

issues.label: Standard for executor commission reasonableness
issues.why: The court must determine the controlling reasonableness factors for fiduciary commissions and whether a flat percentage is permissible without further analysis.

issues.label: Burden of proof on fees
issues.why: The court must decide who bears the initial and ultimate burden to justify attorney fees when an account is challenged and what showing is required.

issues.label: Burden of proof on commissions
issues.why: The court must decide who bears the initial and ultimate burden to justify fiduciary commissions once objected to in an account proceeding.

issues.label: Account is prima facie correct
issues.why: The court must consider the principle that a filed account is prima facie valid and what an objector must prove to surcharge or reduce items.

issues.label: Evidentiary sufficiency for fees
issues.why: The court must determine whether the record (without time records or detailed task evidence) is sufficient to support a finding that the fees were reasonable.

issues.label: Evidentiary sufficiency for commissions
issues.why: The court must determine whether the record is sufficient to support the executor commission as reasonable given limited evidence of the executor’s actual services.

issues.label: Need for time records
issues.why: The court must decide whether lack of contemporaneous timekeeping can be weighed against reasonableness or is immaterial under the applicable standard.

issues.label: Complexity and results obtained
issues.why: The court must evaluate complexity, responsibility assumed, results achieved, and benefit to the estate as part of fee/commission reasonableness.

issues.label: Proportionality to estate size
issues.why: The court must decide whether percentage-based fees become unreasonable as the estate size increases absent corresponding work or risk.

issues.label: Fiduciary duty and self-dealing
issues.why: The court must assess whether the executor’s taking commissions and approving counsel fees complied with fiduciary duties of loyalty and prudent administration.

issues.label: Advance payment of commissions
issues.why: The court must consider whether commissions taken early (before confirmation) were authorized, properly disclosed, and subject to refund/surcharge if excessive.

issues.label: Advance payment of attorney fees
issues.why: The court must consider whether interim/advance fee payments were properly authorized and whether they require later justification at audit.

issues.label: Reasonableness of CPA/accounting fee
issues.why: The court must determine whether the accounting fee paid was necessary, reasonable, and properly chargeable to the estate.

issues.label: Double-compensation concerns
issues.why: The court must consider whether executor services overlapped with paid accounting or legal work creating duplicative compensation.

issues.label: Qualification of counsel as expert
issues.why: The court must decide whether it was proper to qualify estate counsel as an expert to opine on the reasonableness of his own fees and related commissions.

issues.label: Weight vs admissibility of interested expert
issues.why: The court must determine whether counsel’s financial interest affects admissibility, merely weight, or requires corroboration.

issues.label: Need for independent expert testimony
issues.why: The court must consider whether reasonableness required independent evidence beyond the attorney’s self-supporting opinion and local custom.

issues.label: Denial of continuance
issues.why: The court must decide whether denying a continuance (when counsel expected a status hearing) was an abuse of discretion or violated due process.

issues.label: Notice of evidentiary hearing
issues.why: The court must determine whether parties had adequate notice the proceeding would be evidentiary and that expert/records should be prepared.

issues.label: Directed verdict/nonsuit standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard for compulsory nonsuit/directed verdict in an Orphans’ Court audit context and whether it was met.

issues.label: Opportunity to present evidence
issues.why: The court must ensure objectants had a fair opportunity to develop a record supporting unreasonableness, including expert testimony.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: The court must evaluate credibility findings (especially of interested witnesses) and whether they are supported by the record.

issues.label: Findings of fact requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the decree/order contains adequate findings and legal reasoning to permit meaningful appellate review.

issues.label: Application of wrong legal standard
issues.why: The court must determine whether the court erroneously treated Donofrio as dispositive and thereby failed to conduct the required reasonableness analysis.

issues.label: Inheritance tax review relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether Department of Revenue acceptance of returns has any legal significance for Orphans’ Court fee reasonableness determinations.

issues.label: Fiduciary exception to privilege
issues.why: The court must decide whether communications between executor and estate counsel about fees/commissions are discoverable under any fiduciary exception.

issues.label: Privilege waiver and scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether any privilege was waived and, if discoverable, the proper scope and protective limits.

issues.label: Surcharge availability and standard
issues.why: The court must determine what showing is required to surcharge an executor/counsel (loss, breach, or unreasonable compensation) and the proper remedy.

issues.label: Remedy: reduce fees/commissions
issues.why: The court must decide whether the proper relief is reduction/disallowance, disgorgement of overpayments, or other equitable adjustment.

issues.label: Interest on disallowed sums
issues.why: The court must consider whether interest should be charged on excessive commissions/fees paid before confirmation.

issues.label: Effect of original executor’s death
issues.why: The court must determine how the death of the original executor affects proof of services, responsibility for repayment, and administration of objections.

issues.label: Allocation between executors
issues.why: The court must decide whether commissions should be apportioned between original and successor executors based on services performed.

issues.label: Proper party responsibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether repayment/surcharge runs against the estate, the executor’s estate, the successor executor, or counsel, depending on wrongdoing and receipt.

issues.label: Compliance with Pa.O.C. Rule 2.4
issues.why: The court must determine whether the petition for adjudication/statement of proposed distribution complied with procedural requirements.

issues.label: Adequacy of account disclosures
issues.why: The court must decide whether the account adequately described services, bases for fees/commissions, and supporting documentation for informed review.

issues.label: Distribution timing and reserves
issues.why: The court must consider whether distribution should be delayed or reserves held pending resolution of fee objections/appeal.

issues.label: Equitable considerations
issues.why: The court must consider the estate’s overall administration fairness to beneficiaries when approving fiduciary and counsel compensation.
